description_full: Oxford Industries, Inc., an apparel company, designs, sources, markets, and distributes lifestyle products worldwide. The company offers men's and women's sportswear and related products under the Tommy Bahama brand; and women's and girls' dresses and sportswear, scarves, bags, jewelry, and belts, as well as children's apparel, swim, footwear, and licensed products under the Lilly Pulitzer brand. It also licenses Tommy Bahama brand for various products, such as indoor and outdoor furniture, beach chairs, bedding and bath linens, fabrics, leather goods and gifts, headwear, hosiery, sleepwear, shampoo, toiletries, fragrances, cigar accessories, resort operations, and other products; Johnny Was brand that designs, sources, markets and distributes upscale collections of affordable luxury, artisan-inspired bohemian apparel, accessories and home goods; and Lilly Pulitzer for stationery and gift products, home furnishing products, and eyewear. The company distributes its products through southerntide.com, thebeaufortbonnetcompany.com, duckhead.com, and jackrogersusa.com; and specialty retailers, as well as offers product under the Southern Tide, TBBC, Duck Head and Jack Rogers brand name. It offers products through its retail stores, department stores, specialty stores, multi-branded e-commerce retailers, off-price retailers, and other retailers, as well as e-commerce sites. The company operates brand-specific full-price retail stores; Tommy Bahama food and beverage locations; and Tommy Bahama outlet stores. Oxford Industries, Inc. was founded in 1942 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

financial_summary: Oxford Industries, Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $420M market cap on $1.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 15% against a 9% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 57% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $11M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 22.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 6.8% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
